subject: Otorhinolaryngology (ENT)
content: Otorhinolaryngology covers disorders of the ear, nose, throat, head, and neck, including hearing, balance, smell, swallowing, and upper airway functions.

subject: Otorhinolaryngology (ENT)
content: The external ear includes the auricle and external auditory canal and helps collect and direct sound toward the tympanic membrane.

subject: Otorhinolaryngology (ENT)
content: The middle ear contains the tympanic membrane and auditory ossicles, which transmit sound vibrations toward the inner ear.

subject: Otorhinolaryngology (ENT)

subject: Otorhinolaryngology (ENT)
content: The cochlea is the auditory part of the inner ear and converts mechanical sound-related vibrations into neural signals.

subject: Otorhinolaryngology (ENT)

subject: Otorhinolaryngology (ENT)
content: Hearing loss may result from problems involving the outer, middle, or inner ear or auditory pathways and can affect communication and quality of life.

subject: Otorhinolaryngology (ENT)
content: Conductive hearing loss results from impaired transmission of sound through the external or middle ear.

subject: Otorhinolaryngology (ENT)
content: Sensorineural hearing loss involves the inner ear or neural pathways responsible for hearing.

subject: Otorhinolaryngology (ENT)

subject: Otorhinolaryngology (ENT)
content: Otitis externa is inflammation or infection of the external auditory canal and may cause ear pain, tenderness, or discharge.

subject: Otorhinolaryngology (ENT)
content: Otitis media is inflammation or infection involving the middle ear and is particularly common in children.

subject: Otorhinolaryngology (ENT)
content: Chronic ear disease can cause persistent discharge, structural damage, and hearing impairment and may require specialist assessment.

subject: Otorhinolaryngology (ENT)
content: Excessive or impacted earwax can obstruct the ear canal and cause conductive hearing symptoms or discomfort.

subject: Otorhinolaryngology (ENT)

subject: Otorhinolaryngology (ENT)
content: Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo is a common vestibular disorder characterized by brief episodes of vertigo triggered by changes in head position.

subject: Otorhinolaryngology (ENT)
content: The nose conditions inspired air and contributes to smell. The nasal cavity is lined by mucosa and communicates with the paranasal sinuses.

subject: Otorhinolaryngology (ENT)
content: Nasal obstruction may result from mucosal swelling, structural abnormalities, infection, allergy, polyps, or other causes.

subject: Otorhinolaryngology (ENT)
content: Epistaxis is bleeding from the nose and can arise from local nasal causes or systemic factors. Significant or recurrent bleeding requires appropriate assessment.

subject: Otorhinolaryngology (ENT)
content: Rhinosinusitis involves inflammation of the nasal and paranasal sinus mucosa and may produce nasal obstruction, discharge, facial pressure, and reduced smell.

subject: Otorhinolaryngology (ENT)
content: Chronic rhinosinusitis is persistent inflammation of the nose and paranasal sinuses and may be associated with nasal obstruction, discharge, facial symptoms, or reduced smell.

subject: Otorhinolaryngology (ENT)
content: Allergic rhinitis is an inflammatory response of the nasal mucosa to allergens and commonly causes sneezing, itching, nasal discharge, and obstruction.

subject: Otorhinolaryngology (ENT)
content: Allergic rhinitis can affect sleep, concentration, school or work performance, and quality of life.

subject: Otorhinolaryngology (ENT)
content: The pharynx is a muscular passage involved in respiration and swallowing and connects the nasal and oral regions with the laryngeal and esophageal pathways.

subject: Otorhinolaryngology (ENT)

subject: Otorhinolaryngology (ENT)

subject: Otorhinolaryngology (ENT)

subject: Otorhinolaryngology (ENT)
